description: Test your cascade skills: specificity scores, order, and inheritance.

questions.explanation: The id scores 100 vs the class's 10 — higher specificity wins regardless of order.
!important goes inside the declaration, before the semicolon: color: red !important;. It can't sit on the selector.
options: !important is in the wrong place — it goes inside the declaration

questions.explanation: The inherit keyword explicitly takes the parent's value.
questions.prompt: Fill in the keyword that makes the card use its parent's color.

questions.explanation: Specificity scores for each selector type.
questions.prompt: Match each to its specificity weight.
Arrange these selectors from lowest to highest specificity.

questions.code:
p { color: red; }
p { color: blue; }
questions.explanation: Same specificity, so the later rule wins — just like the later JS assignment wins.
questions.prompt: Which JavaScript behaves the same way?

questions.explanation: .alert.urgent scores 20 (two classes) vs .alert's 10 — more classes win.
!important is one token — a space between ! and important breaks it.
Only !important outranks an inline style — nothing else in a stylesheet can.
